newsitem.title: Czech republic: TENNIS-FERREIRA SCRAPES BY FURLAN AT CZECH INDOOR.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-FERREIRA SCRAPES BY FURLAN AT CZECH INDOOR.

text.p: Second seed Wayne Ferreira struggled past Italy's Renzo Furlan 7-5 4-6 6-4 in the first round of the $475,000 Czech Indoor Open on Tuesday.

In other action, fifth seed Todd Martin easily disposed of Slovakia's Jan Kroslak 6-3 6-4, while eighth seed Bohdan Ulihrach fought back in the last set to defeat his Davis Cup teammate Daniel Vacek 6-2 3-6 7-5.

After crashing out of the first round in each of the past two weeks, the world number seven Ferreira looked shaky at times, committing a rash of unforced errors that left the match even after two sets.
But another early exit for the South African would have seriously jeopardised his chances of qualifying for the ATP Tour World Championship in Hannover, Germany at the end of the year.

"It's always a tough match against Renzo, he has a game that is suited well against mine," said Ferreira, who currently holds the eighth and final spot for Hannover with Boris Becker, slated to play in Ostrava on Wednesday, just 46 points behind.
"In the third set the early break was key, but even when you're on top against him, he's always fighting back."
Martin, ranked 11th in the world, found the going much easier, however, breaking Kroslak early in each set and saving both break points his opponent managed.
Ulihrach also looked set for an easy win, dominating the first set, but Vacek came charging back to even the match and broke to start the third set.
But Ulihrach, on the verge of losing in the tenth game fought back, regaining the break he lost earlier, and then broke again in the final game to take the set.
